Change your own password, which clears a forced change. The session gets a new token

get.description: The requirement's history, newest first (`?before=` the previous page's `next_cursor`).

post.description:
Create a requirement: the next `RQ` number, `draft`, revision 1, at the bottom of its
siblings. 404 for a `parent_id` outside the project; 422 on `title` (`missing`) and on
`restriction_categories` (`project_only`: `export_controlled` is set on the project).

get.description:
The project's requirements for the tree, siblings in rank order: complete up to 2,000,
with `truncated` above it (DL-159).
The requirement, with the actions the caller may take on it.

patch.description:
Change the fields sent. 409 on a stale `version`; a new revision only when the title or
description changes. `status` `approved`: 403 without `requirement.approve_manually`, else
422 `use_approve`; `reporter_id` needs `requirement.reassign_reporter`, 422
`account_inactive` or `not_member`.

delete.description:
Move the requirement to the trash: its children promoted to its parent (`promote`, the
default) or deleted with it (`delete`, 403 if the caller may not delete each of them); a
pending approval request on it is cancelled.

put.description:
Set the requirement's restriction level and categories (no `version`, DL-162): raising
needs `requirement.raise_restriction`, lowering `requirement.lower_restriction`. 422 on
`level` (`below_project`) and on `categories` (`project_only`).

post.description:
Move the requirement under `parent_id` (null: the top level), just after `after_id` or
just before `before_id`, or to the bottom. 404 for a parent outside the project; 422 on
`parent_id` (`cycle`), `after_id` or `before_id` (`not_sibling`), and `before_id` with both
(`conflict`).

Bring the requirement back from the trash with the descendants deleted with it (403 if
the caller may not restore each of them); at the bottom of the top level if its parent is
still in the trash. 404 for one not in the trash.

get.description: The project's deleted items the caller may restore, newest first.

The requirement's revisions, newest first (`?before=` the previous page's
`next_cursor`).

One revision's title, description, change note, and author; 404 for a number the
requirement doesn't have.

post.description:
Request approval of the requirement's current revision from the named approvers. 404 for
an approver without access to the project; 422 on `approver_ids` (`duplicate`,
`account_inactive`) and on the body (`pending_exists`: one pending request at a time).

get.description: The requirement's approval requests, newest first, with their approvers.

The approval request, with the actions the caller may take on it; 404 for a deleted
requirement's.

post.description:
Cancel the pending request; 422 on `id` (`not_pending`) for one already decided or
cancelled.

AccessKind.title: AccessKind
AccessKind.description:
Content or management (design-doc §3.1, §5): how each action is marked, and what an
inherited admin keeps on an export-controlled project without an explicit membership.

AccessReason.title: AccessReason
AccessReason.description: Why someone reaches an org or a project (design-doc §5, "Access review"; DL-72).

AccessReview.title: AccessReview
AccessReview.description:
The per-person access review (design-doc §5): every org and project the person reaches,
and why. Orgs sorted by name, projects by key.

Action.title: Action
Action.description: The real actions (DL-44, DL-45, DL-56; each area adds its own).

ActivityEntry.title: ActivityEntry
ActivityEntry.description:
One change, newest first in its feed. Names are resolved by the server at read time, so a
former member's name stays; `*_is_active` false shows the "Deactivated" badge. `changed_by_*`
is null when an app CLI command made the change. `old_value_*` and `new_value_*` name the
user in a user field (`reporter_id`, `assignee_id`, `reviewer_id`, `lead_id`, `approver_id`),
and are null for any other field.

ApprovalRead.title: ApprovalRead
ApprovalRead.description: One approver's row; `approver_is_active` false shows the "Deactivated" badge.

ApprovalRequestCreate.title: ApprovalRequestCreate
ApprovalRequestCreate.description:
A request bound to the requirement's current revision. `approver_ids`: 1 to 50 distinct
users with access to the project (a repeat is a 422 `duplicate`, someone without access a
404, a deactivated one a 422 `account_inactive`; DL-226).

ApprovalRequestItem.title: ApprovalRequestItem
ApprovalRequestItem.description: A request on the requirement's list, newest first (DL-227), with its approvers.

ApprovalRequestRead.title: ApprovalRequestRead
ApprovalRequestRead.description: One request, with the actions the caller may take on it.

DeletedChildren.title: DeletedChildren
DeletedChildren.description: What a requirement's delete does with its children (design-doc §9).

EmailCheck.title: EmailCheck
EmailCheck.description: Whether an account has this email; never whose (DL-66).

ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody
ErrorBody.description:
The body of every error response. `details` depends on `code` (e.g. `fields` for
`validation_error`).

HealthRead.title: HealthRead
HealthRead.description:
A healthy response. When the database is unreachable the endpoint returns 503 with the
standard error body instead (`service_unavailable`).

MeOrg.title: MeOrg
MeOrg.description:
An org the user sees (design-doc §4, "Visibility"), for the org menu. `role` is null
when the user sees it without an org membership (through a project, or as an admin above
it).

MeRead.title: MeRead
MeRead.description: The signed-in user: `GET /api/auth/me`, and the sign-in response.

MeWorkspace.title: MeWorkspace
MeWorkspace.description:
A workspace the user is staff of, or, for a system admin, any workspace (`role` null where
they aren't staff; DL-46), with the workspace-level actions they may take there (DL-45).

MemberAdd.title: MemberAdd
MemberAdd.description: Add an existing account, found by email (design-doc §4: the email comes first).

MemberCandidate.title: MemberCandidate
MemberCandidate.description: Someone the picker offers: an org member or staff member not yet on the project.

MemberRead.title: MemberRead
MemberRead.description: An org member, with the actions the caller may take on this row.

MemberRoleUpdate.title: MemberRoleUpdate
MemberRoleUpdate.description:
`new_owner_id`: when an owner steps down, a current member to make owner in the same
change (the last owner needs one; DL-59).

ModuleGuidance.title: ModuleGuidance
ModuleGuidance.description: Static guidance for module choice (design-doc §1.1; DL-76).

MyWork.title: MyWork
MyWork.description: `GET /api/me/work` (design-doc §11; DL-76): every section in one response.

NewUser.title: NewUser
NewUser.description:
A new account: the admin passes on the temporary password, which the user must change
at their first sign-in.

OrgCreate.title: OrgCreate
OrgCreate.description:
An org and its first owner: exactly one of `owner_id` (an existing active user) and
`new_owner` (a new account).

OwnProfileUpdate.title: OwnProfileUpdate
OwnProfileUpdate.description:
The signed-in user's change to their own profile: their email isn't theirs to change in v1
(design-doc §4).

PasswordPolicyRead.title: PasswordPolicyRead
PasswordPolicyRead.description:
`GET /api/auth/password-policy` (DL-91): the requirements, in order. The length cap isn't
listed; the server refuses it.

PasswordRequirement.title: PasswordRequirement
PasswordRequirement.description:
One requirement a new password must meet: `code` is the 422 field error `type` it prevents
(DL-94), `label` is written for users, and `value` is the number it needs, where it has one.

PasswordReset.title: PasswordReset
PasswordReset.description: The temporary password an admin sets; the user must change it at next sign-in.

ProjectAccessEntry.title: ProjectAccessEntry
ProjectAccessEntry.description: One person who reaches the project: their explicit role, if any, and why they reach it.

ProjectAccessReview.title: ProjectAccessReview
ProjectAccessReview.description:
The per-project access review (design-doc §5; DL-78): everyone who reaches the project,
sorted by name.

ProjectCreate.title: ProjectCreate
ProjectCreate.description: A new project in an org (DL-76). Without `enabled_modules`, it's seeded from the type.

ProjectItem.title: ProjectItem
ProjectItem.description: A project in a list: the org's projects, and My work's projects section.

ProjectMemberAdd.title: ProjectMemberAdd
ProjectMemberAdd.description:
Exactly one of `user_id` (from the picker) and `email` (email first, design-doc §4).
`join_org` confirms adding an account from outside the org and the staff to the org too
(DL-78).

ProjectMemberRead.title: ProjectMemberRead
ProjectMemberRead.description: An explicit project membership, with the actions the caller may take on this row.

ProjectModule.title: ProjectModule
ProjectModule.description:
Modules a project may enable. Only shipped-or-v1 modules are allowed values; each v2
module is added (with the `enabled_modules` CHECK) when it ships (schema-doc, `project`).

ProjectUpdate.title: ProjectUpdate
ProjectUpdate.description: Only the fields sent change; `lead_id: null` clears the lead. The key never changes.

RequirementCreate.title: RequirementCreate
RequirementCreate.description:
A new requirement: `draft`, reported by the caller, at the bottom of its siblings.
`parent_id` is a requirement in the same project (anything else is a 404); the restriction
may raise the item's level and add categories (design-doc §3.1; `export_controlled` is
project-only).

RequirementItem.title: RequirementItem
RequirementItem.description: A row of the requirement tree.

RequirementMove.title: RequirementMove
RequirementMove.description:
`POST …/requirements/{number}/move`: under `parent_id` (null: the top level), just after
the sibling `after_id` or just before `before_id`, or with neither at the bottom of the
parent's children (design-doc §6, "Manual ordering").

RequirementRead.title: RequirementRead
RequirementRead.description:
One requirement, with the actions the caller may take on it. "Approved · modified" is
derived: `approved_revision_id` set and not `current_revision_id` (design-doc §6.1).

RequirementRestrictionUpdate.title: RequirementRestrictionUpdate
RequirementRestrictionUpdate.description:
`PUT …/requirements/{number}/restriction` (DL-162): `level` (null: inherit the project's)
and `categories` replace the current ones. No `version` (DL-168).

RequirementTree.title: RequirementTree
RequirementTree.description:
The project's requirements in `(rank, id)` order, siblings in rank order (the client
nests them by `parent_id`); at most 2,000, with `truncated` above it (DL-159).

RequirementUpdate.title: RequirementUpdate
RequirementUpdate.description:
Only the fields sent change. `version` is the one the caller read (a stale one is a
409). A new revision, with `change_note`, only when `title` or `description_md` changes
(design-doc §6.1). `status` may not be `approved` (DL-161); `reporter_id` needs
`requirement.reassign_reporter` (DL-211).

RestrictionUpdate.title: RestrictionUpdate
RestrictionUpdate.description:
`PUT /api/projects/{key}/restriction` (DL-81): `level` (null: None) and
`categories` replace the current ones. Adding `export_controlled` also needs
`export_control_confirmed` and `confirmed_member_ids`, the project's current explicit
members.

RevisionItem.title: RevisionItem
RevisionItem.description:
A row of the requirement's revision list, newest first (design-doc §6.1); the author's
name is resolved at read time, and `created_by_is_active` false shows the "Deactivated"
badge.

RevisionRead.title: RevisionRead
RevisionRead.description: One revision's snapshot, for the compare (DL-145: computed in the browser).

SlugAvailability.title: SlugAvailability
SlugAvailability.description:
Whether a slug can be used: `problem` is the slug rule's problem (`reserved`,
`too_short`, ...), or `taken`; null when it's available.

StaffAdd.title: StaffAdd
StaffAdd.description: Add an existing account, found by email (design-doc §4: the email comes first).

StaffRead.title: StaffRead
StaffRead.description: A workspace staff member, with the actions the caller may take on this row.

StaffRoleUpdate.title: StaffRoleUpdate
StaffRoleUpdate.description:
`new_owner_id`: when an owner steps down, current staff to make owner in the same change
(the last owner needs one; DL-59).

TrashItem.title: TrashItem
TrashItem.description: A row of the project's trash: the item, who deleted it, and when (design-doc §9).

TrashItemType.title: TrashItemType
TrashItemType.description: What the trash lists (design-doc §9; tasks and test cases join in Slices 3 and 5).

UserRow.title: UserRow
UserRow.description:
A user as the workspace users list shows them (DL-72), with the account actions the caller
may take on them.

UserUpdate.title: UserUpdate
UserUpdate.description: An admin's change to a user's profile: any subset of the three (DL-72).

UsernameSuggestion.title: UsernameSuggestion
UsernameSuggestion.description: An available username suggested from a name, or null when none can be made (DL-66).

ReservedSlug.title: ReservedSlug
ReservedSlug.description: Top-level browser routes: no workspace or org slug may be one.
